questions.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}-\frac{1}{z}\,dx+x\,dy+dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the helix parametrized by $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+t\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k$ for $t\in [0,\pi ].$
questions.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=t,\,z(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,k \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}-\frac{1}{z}\,dx+x\,dy+dz & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }-\frac{1}{z}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(-\frac{1}{z}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }-\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot 1+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }1+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =(t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\pi +2\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi -0 \\  & =\pi \end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}(x+y)\,dx+x\,dy,$ where $C$ is a portion of the parabola parametrized by $r(t)=2t\,i+(2-{t}^{2})\,j$ for $t\in [0,1].$
questions.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=2t,\,y(t)=2-{t}^{2}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-{t}^{2})\,j \\  & =2\,i-2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}(x+y)\,dx+x\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(x+y)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[(x+y)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}]dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2t+2-{t}^{2})\cdot 2+2t\cdot (-2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}-6{t}^{2}+4t+4\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[-2{t}^{3}+2{t}^{2}+4t]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(-2+2+4)-0 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}{y}^{2}\,dx+x\,dy+z\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the line $r(t)=t\,i+2t\,j+3t\,k$ for $t\in [0,5]?$
questions.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=t,\,y(t)=2t,\,z(t)=3t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t)\,k \\  & =\,i+2\,j+3\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}{y}^{2}\,dx+x\,dy+z\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{5}{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{5}({y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{5}4{t}^{2}\cdot (1)+t\cdot (2)+3t\cdot (3)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{5}4{t}^{2}+11t\,dt\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}xy\,dx+y\,dy+z\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the curve $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+{t}^{3}\,k$ for $t\in [3,5]?$
questions.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=t,\,y(t)={t}^{2},\,z(t)={t}^{3}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\,k \\  & =\,i+2t\,j+3{t}^{2}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}xy\,dx+y\,dy+z\,dz & ={\int }_{3}^{5}xy\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}(xy\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}{t}^{3}\cdot (1)+{t}^{2}\cdot (2t)+{t}^{3}\cdot (3{t}^{2})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}3{t}^{5}+3{t}^{3}\,dt \\  & =3{\int }_{3}^{5}{t}^{5}+{t}^{3}\,dt\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}(x+y)\,dx+y\,dy,$ where $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)=(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1)\,i+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1)\,j$ for $t\in [-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1,\,y(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1)\,j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}(x+y)\,dx+y\,dy & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}(x+y)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}((x+y)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+1+\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1)\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-{sin}^{2}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}-{sin}^{2}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$
